plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Tall, sun-chasing stems carry broad golden-yellow petals around dark, seed-packed centers. In late summer, fields and roadsides across the American Southwest fill with their bright faces, and bees and goldfinches crowd in.
plants.location: Southwestern United States, including the high desert around Santa Fe, New Mexico
plants.funFact: Each sunflower head is really hundreds of tiny individual flowers. The outer ray petals are only the showy fringe, and every small disc floret in the center can become a seed.

plants.name: Eutrochium purpureum
plants.description: A towering native wildflower of meadows and woodland edges. Its domed clusters of dusky pink-mauve flowers float above whorled leaves and smell faintly of vanilla. Butterflies, especially swallowtails and monarchs, flock to it in late summer.
plants.funFact: Its odd name is often traced to a Native American healer called Joe Pye, who reportedly used the plant to treat fevers.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Australia's national floral emblem. In the last weeks of winter, the tree is covered in fluffy, honey-scented golden pom-poms that light up the bush against gray-green foliage.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring, around July to October
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: What look like petals are actually clusters of showy stamens. Australians celebrate Wattle Day on September 1, the unofficial first day of spring.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest bloom in the protea family. It is a huge, artichoke-like flower head with a crown of silky-tipped pink bracts, and it grows on the fynbos slopes of the Cape.
plants.bloomingSeason: Roughly July to October (late winter into spring in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: It is South Africa's national flower. Its thick underground stem, called a lignotuber, helps it resprout after the wildfires that regularly sweep through the fynbos.
